top_choice_rationale: P001 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) rewards three separable originating ideas that later work takes as given: the tractable time-dependent pricing device, staggered contracts with the policy-rule benchmark, and the microfounded welfare-based framework for evaluating policy. The work is 25 to 45 years old and has shaped how monetary policy is analysed. The 2022 prize covered banking and financial crises, not this core. The main costs are real. Any trio leaves out Galí, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets. Priority questions involving Fischer and Phelps are unresolved. The micro evidence on state dependence and the post-2021 inflation limit what a citation can claim. A citation worded around the originating ideas and the framework as an analytical benchmark answers most of this. P002 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) is second because its credit boundary is cleaner and the work is mature. Against it, cross-country identification is weaker, the 2024 institutions prize is a neighbour, and whether Besley is separable is a judgement. P003 (Helpman, Melitz) is third. It has a clean two-name core and its predictions have been tested on firm-level data. Its costs are that Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum are outside the entry, the welfare results depend on functional-form assumptions, and it follows the 2008 trade prize. I rank no award last because all three proposals describe mature, substantive achievements. Support counts are not evidence of merit, and I have not independently verified priority or empirical claims.
recusal_note: No tie to the credited names in B001, B006 or B021 is apparent from my profile. Disclosed, not adjudicated: I am a Lund colleague of Kerstin Enflo (B006 supporter). I am an SSE affiliate alongside Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg. I co-authored COVID policy work with SSE economists. My field of market design is not close to B001. I gave the 2020 presentation speech, which does not establish a private preference here.
